speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are here for a chronic wound on your right lower leg. To begin, can you tell me how long this wound has been present and if you have a history of diabetes or peripheral artery disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. The long-standing swelling and previous DVT strongly suggest venous insufficiency, but I need to rule out arterial causes. Do you experience any pain in your legs while walking that improves with rest, or do you notice coolness or hair loss on that leg?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of claudication symptoms makes arterial disease less likely, pointing further toward a venous etiology. Does the wound drain fluid, and have you noticed any changes in the skin color, such as darkening or hardening, around the wound site?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Deep vein thrombosis in the right leg 5 years prior. No other significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as an accountant.

speaker: Doctor
text: The wound drainage and skin changes you described are consistent with venous stasis. To confirm the diagnosis and assess the severity of the venous insufficiency, I would like to order a vascular ultrasound of the right leg. REQUEST TEST: Venous_Duplex_Ultrasound_Leg
